basis: Disease of the cardiac conduction system; cardiac muscle is cardiovascular, not skeletal muscle.
Inherited serine biosynthesis defect; developmental impairment, seizures or other neurologic dysfunction occur in most symptomatic patients.
Prolymphocytic leukemia involving the spleen; both leukemic blood cells and the spleen as a blood organ fall under haematologic.
Definition specifies actual ALK-related neuroblastoma, a tumor of sympathetic neural tissue, rather than susceptibility alone.
Developmental delay/intellectual disability and fifth-finger skeletal abnormalities occur in 4/4 reported patients; cardiac and laryngeal defects only 1/4.
Nonfunctioning adenoma arising in the pituitary endocrine gland; common damaging involvement of another axis is not established for this subtype.
Inherited calcium-sensing disorder causing usually benign hypercalcemia; hypocalciuria does not imply renal damage, and stones or pancreatitis are uncommon.
Brain malformations and severe neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; optic nerve hypoplasia is defining and occurs in 80-99%.
Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma arising in the urinary bladder.
Malignant tumor arising from the superior vena cava wall; vascular smooth muscle belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Rifampicin-resistant mycobacterial infection; active tuberculosis directly involves and damages lungs in the large majority, roughly 80% or more.
Peroxisomal disorder; predominant rhizomelic chondrodysplasia phenotypes cause skeletal dysplasia, cataracts and neurologic impairment in most; milder forms vary.
Inherited cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; occasional transient visual loss does not establish common ocular damage.
Medulloblastoma occupying the brainstem.
Familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; reported arrhythmia and valve abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Contagious ectoparasitic infestation of skin and hair; its cutaneous location and infectious mechanism define the disease.
Acquired disorder of neurologic coordination; immune-mediated disease is only one subgroup and does not define the umbrella.
Acute leukemia is a malignant disease of blood-forming cells; X-linked inheritance does not establish another affected organ.
Pulmonary venous/capillary disease with hypertension and proliferative infiltration of lung interstitium; both vascular and pulmonary injury define it.
Neuronal-glial tumor involving cerebral cortex and leptomeninges; hypotropia alone does not establish direct ocular damage.
Adrenal cortisol excess causes hypertension in ~80%, myopathy/bone loss in >50%, and skin atrophy/easy bruising in roughly 50-80%; diabetes is separately coded.
Heart defects, craniosynostosis/ankylosis and developmental disability define it; tracheal malformations occur in 30-79%; lesser hair/palatal anomalies omitted at cap.
Broad umbrella of congenital sexual/reproductive development abnormalities; endocrine gland dysfunction is not required and cannot be assigned across the group.
Complete open spinal dysraphism involves the vertebral column and exposed malformed spinal cord; urinary sequelae are not assumed in this usually lethal form.
Ectopic adrenocortical tumor produces aldosterone; sustained hypertension is obligate (100%) and defining; variable ectopic sites do not establish renal involvement.
